title: avg() computes the mean of a numeric field
body:
_function_

Computes the arithmetic mean of a numeric field over the incoming events (per group inside groupBy).

Syntax:

```
avg([as], field)
```

- `as` (string, optional, default '_avg') — Name for the output field (optional).
- `field` (string, required) — Field whose numeric values are averaged.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([ComputerName], function=avg(field=RssBytes, as=avg_rss))
```
Average value per host.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:sum`, `cql:function:groupBy`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-avg.html (reviewed 2026-09-15)

title: bucket() splits the search interval into time slices and aggregates each
body:
_function_

Splits the query time interval into buckets and runs aggregate functions per bucket, optionally per value of the grouping fields. Each output row carries the bucket start time in _bucket.

Syntax:

```
bucket([buckets], [field], [function], [limit], [minSpan], [span], [timezone], [unit])
```

- `buckets` (integer, optional) — Number of buckets the query interval is split into; range 0..1500, minimum 1.
- `field` (array of strings, optional) — Fields to group by; multiple allowed.
- `function` (array of aggregate functions, optional, default 'count(as=_count)') — Aggregates to run per group; multiple are combined as in stats().
- `limit` (integer, optional, default '10') — Cap on the number of series (up to 500); the series with the top function output are kept.
- `minSpan` (long, optional) — Minimum allowed bucket span as relative time (e.g. 1hour); cannot exceed the search interval.
- `span` (relative time, optional, default 'auto') — Time span per bucket; auto sizes buckets dynamically.
- `timezone` (timezone, optional) — Time zone for bucketing.
- `unit` (array of strings, optional) — Unit conversion per column; length 1 or equal to the length of function.

- Caveat: _bucket holds the bucket start time in milliseconds (UTC).
- Caveat: span accepts only fixed-length durations; calendar-based units are not available, and bucket edges cannot be anchored to a specific time unit.
- Caveat: Series are selected by the numerical output of the functions, not by series name; limit keeps the top-N series.
- Caveat: The output can contain one more bucket than requested because trailing data is always included (24 buckets over one day can return 25).
- Caveat: The docs point to timeChart() as an alternative; the extra trailing bucket can affect a Time Chart widget fed by bucket().

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | bucket(span=1h, function=count())
```

Process-creation events per hour; one row per bucket with _bucket and _count.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | bucket(span=1d, field=FileName, function=count(), limit=20)
```

Per-day counts per process name; limit caps the number of series (max 500).

Example (ANTI-PATTERN — do not use):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | bucket(span=1h) by FileName
```

SQL/SPL-style by clause does not exist; group with field=.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:timeChart`, `cql:troubleshooting:timechart-series-limit`, `cql:function:groupBy`, `cql:troubleshooting:bucket-drops-fields`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-bucket.html

title: collect() gathers distinct values of fields into one event
body:
_function_

Aggregate that collects the distinct values of the named fields. With multival=true (default) values are concatenated into one string using separator; with false each value is output on its own row. Typically used inside groupBy().

Syntax:

```
collect(fields, [limit], [multival], [separator])
```

- `fields` (array of fieldnames, required) — Field names to collect values from; the argument name can be omitted.
- `limit` (integer, optional, default '2000') — Cap on distinct values collected (at least 1).
- `multival` (boolean, optional, default 'true') — false outputs one value per row; true outputs a single concatenated string.
- `separator` (string, optional, default '\\n') — Separator between values when concatenating (multival=true).

- Caveat: The order of collected values is undefined.
- Caveat: Collection is capped by limit and by a memory allocation: 10 MiB at top level, 1 MiB in other contexts such as a subquery or a sub-aggregator.
- Caveat: If either cap is exceeded the function returns partial results and shows a warning.
- Caveat: Output fields keep the input field names; collect() has no as parameter.
- Caveat: @timestamp can be collected only when each event carries a single timestamp; otherwise copy it to another field first, or use selectLast() or limit=1 when one value is enough.
- Caveat: Use on smaller datasets; it returns the full set and can run out of memory on large ones.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([aid], function=[collect([FileName]), selectLast([ComputerName])])
```
Per host: distinct process names plus last-seen hostname.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([aid], function=collect([FileName], separator=", ", limit=50))
```
Comma-separated list capped at 50 distinct values.

Example (ANTI-PATTERN — do not use):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([aid], function=collect([FileName], as=names))
```
collect() has no as parameter; output keeps the input field name.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:groupBy`, `cql:function:selectLast`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-collect.html (reviewed 2026-10-21)

title: count() counts events or distinct field values
body:
_function_

Counts events streaming through the pipeline, or (with field=) only events that contain that field. count(distinct=true, field=X) counts unique values of X; with many distinct values the result is an estimate, not exact. For an exact distinct count use groupBy([X], limit=max) | count().

Syntax:

```
count([as], [distinct], [field])
```

- `as` (string, optional, default '_count') — The name of the output field.
- `distinct` (boolean, optional, default 'false') — Defines whether to count incoming values, or count only the distinct (unique) values for a given field.
- `field` (string, optional) — Restricts the count to events that contain this field.

- Caveat: distinct=true requires a field; for many distinct values the result is an estimate (docs: typical standard error under 2%, no guarantee on relative error, larger deviation below 100 distinct values).
- Caveat: Exact distinct count: groupBy([field], limit=max) | count(). Without limit=max the default cap of 20,000 groups drops the rest silently, even though the stage reports no error; see cql:performance:groupby-explicit-limit.
- Caveat: dc() is not a CQL function and is not in the documented function list; use count(field, distinct=true) or the exact groupBy method.
- Caveat: Use inside groupBy(function=count(...)) to count per group.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=UserLogon | count(as=logon_count)
```

Total matching events into a named field.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest | groupBy([ComputerName], function=count(field=DomainName, distinct=true, as=unique_domains))
```

Distinct count per host; the per-group value is an estimate at high cardinality.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 FileName=powershell.exe | groupBy([aid], limit=max) | count(as=distinct_hosts)
```

Exact number of distinct hosts that ran powershell.exe: count the groups. limit=max raises the group cap to its documented maximum; a population above that still truncates.

Example (ANTI-PATTERN — do not use):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([FileName], function=dc(aid))
```

dc() is not a CQL function; use count(aid, distinct=true) (estimate) or the exact groupBy method.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:groupBy`, `cql:troubleshooting:distinct-estimate`, `cql:performance:groupby-explicit-limit`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-count.html; https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-groupby.html

title: groupBy() aggregates into groups and can silently truncate
body:
_function_

groupBy() groups events on one or more key fields and applies an aggregate function to each group. The documented GroupDefaultLimit is 20,000 groups; when a query yields more, groupBy drops the excess and returns an incomplete result instead of failing. It can truncate earlier when QueryCoordinatorMemoryLimit is reached. A later head() or sort() cannot bring back groups already lost upstream.

Syntax:

```
groupBy([field, ...], function=aggregate(...))
```

- `field` (field or array of fields, required) — The field(s) to group by.
- `function` (aggregate function, optional) — Aggregation applied per group, e.g. count(), sum(). Defaults to count().
- `limit` (int, optional) — Maximum number of groups to return; increasing it raises memory cost. The documented GroupDefaultLimit is 20,000, but QueryCoordinatorMemoryLimit can truncate earlier.

- Caveat: Silent truncation: exceeding GroupDefaultLimit=20,000 yields incomplete results with no error, and QueryCoordinatorMemoryLimit can impose a lower memory-bound limit that varies with the query and merge.
- Caveat: Narrow cardinality before grouping. top() is a shortcut for top-values questions but is approximate on high-cardinality fields (see cql:function:top); for an exact ranking raise the cap with limit=max and sort().
- Caveat: The documented default and maximum group counts are product defaults; reverify the current numbers against the docs and do not assume a deployment's configured limits match the defaults.
- Caveat: An explicit limit= set below the real group count drops groups inside groupBy, before any sort()/head()/top() and with no error, so the ranking is wrong. Raise it (limit=max) before sort(), or narrow the filter; top() is only an approximation. See cql:performance:groupby-explicit-limit.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | groupBy([ComputerName], function=count(as=proc_count)) | sort(proc_count, order=desc, limit=100)
```

Group by host, count, then cap the returned rows with sort(limit=).

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language / Group-count default documented as GroupDefaultLimit=20,000; QueryCoordinatorMemoryLimit can truncate earlier, and exact behavior is version-dependent.

See also: `cql:performance:result-caps`, `cql:function:top`, `cql:performance:groupby-explicit-limit`, `cql:troubleshooting:groupby-missing-keys`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-groupby.html; https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/query-operation-limits.html

title: max() returns the largest value of a field
body:
_function_

Returns the maximum value of the given field over the incoming events (per group inside groupBy). On @timestamp it yields the most recent event.

Syntax:

```
max([as], field)
```

- `as` (string, optional, default '_max') — Name of output field.
- `field` (string, required) — Field whose numeric values are compared.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=UserLogon | groupBy([UserName], function=max(@timestamp, as=last_seen))
```
Most recent logon per user.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:min`, `cql:function:groupBy`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-max.html (reviewed 2026-09-15)

title: min() returns the smallest value of a field
body:
_function_

Returns the minimum value of the given field over the incoming events (per group inside groupBy). Works on numbers and on @timestamp to find the earliest event.

Syntax:

```
min([as], field)
```

- `as` (string, optional, default '_min') — Name of output field.
- `field` (string, required) — Field whose numeric values are compared.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=UserLogon | groupBy([UserName], function=min(@timestamp, as=first_seen))
```
Earliest logon per user.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:max`, `cql:function:groupBy`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-min.html (reviewed 2026-09-15)

title: selectFromMax() returns the event holding the largest value of a field
body:
_function_

Aggregate that returns one event, with only the fields listed in include, taken from the event where field is largest. A way to get the latest value of a field without sorting.

Syntax:

```
selectFromMax(field, include)
```

- `field` (fieldname, required) — Field whose largest value picks the event; the argument name may be left out.
- `include` (array of fieldnames, required) — Fields copied into the returned event.

- Caveat: Output is zero or one event containing only the fields listed in include.
- Caveat: If several events tie, one is returned randomly (non-deterministic).
- Caveat: Incompatible with Filter Alerts.

Example (valid):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | selectFromMax(@timestamp, include=[aid, ComputerName, FileName, @timestamp])
```
Single event with the maximum @timestamp and the listed fields.

Example (ANTI-PATTERN — do not use):

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | selectFromMax(@timestamp)
```
include is required.

Applicability: CrowdStrike Query Language

See also: `cql:function:selectFromMin`, `cql:function:selectLast`, `cql:function:groupBy`

Sources: https://library.humio.com/crowdstrike-query-language/functions-selectfrommax.html (reviewed 2026-10-21)

```
selectFromMin(field, include)
```

```
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | selectFromMin(@timestamp, include=[aid, ComputerName, FileName, @timestamp])
```
Single event with the minimum @timestamp and the listed fields.
